newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on hedges, commission selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on hedges, commission selling.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower on hedges and commission house selling, traders said.

"Commission houses are selling, there's hedges. Funds covered July shorts, the Pools bought July scale down late, Cargill and RBC-DS are buying new crop," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin fell to +0.96 Wednesday from +4.35 Tuesday. About 800 July-Nov spread from $27 to $30, 900 July Aug from $3.50 to $4, 50 Aug-Nov at $24.
July canola lost $2.10 to $385.90, August set a new low at $381.50 but ended down $3.20 at $381.70 while September lost $5.80 to $357.70 after it set a new contract low of $356.50.
July flax rose $0.50 to $330 as PCTS sold, November down $0.20 at $304.30.
RBC-DS bought 35 July oats down US$1 at US$113, RBC-DS and PCTS bought 55 December oats up US$1.10 to US$108.80.

Commercial liquidation pushed July western barley down $1.50 to a new low of $125. October fell $1.10 to $128.40 after setting a new low at $128.20 as commercial bought scale down. Benson Quinn sold July-Oct at $3, traders said.
July feed wheat lost $1.50 to $150.50 on commercial liquidation. July-Oct at $3, Oct-Dec $3. Peas did not trade.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
